answer.text: Short-term liquidity — the ability to meet current obligations from current assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities. It measures short-term liquidity. The Trap: Current ratio is a liquidity measure, not a profitability or valuation metric. Note: A ratio above 1 means current assets exceed current liabilities; a very low ratio may require deeper analysis. A current ratio below 1 is not necessarily a red flag in every cash-and-credit situation, and negative working capital can be acceptable for firms with strong customer and supplier bargaining power.
